title: BOD 26-04: Vulnerability Severity Does Not Matter
content_md: Introduction This year, the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) published Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 26-04, “Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk” [1]. The directive prioritizes vulnerability remediation based on four key risk factors, representing a significant shift in how organizations approach vulnerability management. Rather than prioritizing remediation solely based on vulnerability severity, organizations will need to consider the broader risk a vulnerability poses to their environment. Reasoning Behind BOD 26-04 The primary reason BOD 26-04 was created is to address the challenge organizations face in remediating vulnerabilities quickly while prioritizing those that pose the “real risk” to their environment. In the past, identifying patching priorities was relatively straightforward: Just patch the critical vulnerabilities,” right? Prioritizing vulnerabilities based solely on severity makes vulnerability identification and reporting easy. Remediation, however, is much more difficult. Intentional or not, BOD 26-04 shifts that dynamic. Vulnerability reporting and prioritization become significantly more complex because organizations must evaluate multiple risk factors rather than relying on severity alone.
